note: Source registry for the Universal Wisdom Library. ingestion_status records what this project has actually done with a source, not what the source permits. A source marked restricted or unavailable is linked for reference and is not copied into the corpus.

sources.source_reliability_notes: Official and authoritative: the Reference Library is the Bahá’í International Community's own publication of the Bahá’í writings, and the English texts it serves are the authorised translations. sources.editorial_notes: Used for the writings of Bahá’u’lláh and ‘Abdu’l-Bahá held as streamed works: the Hidden Words, the Kitáb-i-Aqdas, the Kitáb-i-Íqán, The Seven Valleys and the Four Valleys, Gleanings from the Writings of Bahá’u’lláh, Some Answered Questions, the Epistle to the Son of the Wolf, the Tablets of Bahá’u’lláh and Prayers and Meditations. Access was authorised by the project owner on 2026-10-26. The texts remain the Community's copyright: the library streams them from bahai.org, keeps the copyright notice with every chapter it shows, and does not relicense them. Nothing is copied into the local corpus, and the import cache holds only the paragraph index that the search and reader need.
sources.review_note: Approved for streamed display on 2026-10-26. Only the authorised English texts published by the Reference Library are used; the Community's copyright notice and the work's title are shown with every chapter, and no Bahá’í text is copied into the local corpus.

sources.source_reliability_notes: Large Protestant-oriented collection; editions vary in quality and provenance. The Ante-Nicene and Nicene and Post-Nicene Fathers are the Edinburgh and Oxford series the library already streams; their English translations are public domain, while some introductions and the SBL Greek New Testament that the library now lists are in copyright and are not imported.
sources.editorial_notes: The 38-volume Ante-Nicene and Nicene and Post-Nicene Fathers are imported as streamed works, one section page at a time: the Apostolic Fathers, the apologists, Clement of Alexandria, Origen, Tertullian, Hippolytus, Cyprian, Lactantius, Methodius, Arnobius, Eusebius, Athanasius, Basil, Gregory of Nyssa and Nazianzen, Chrysostom, Jerome, Ambrose, Augustine, Leo and Gregory the Great, John of Damascus, Cassian, Vincent of Lerins, the seven ecumenical councils, the New Testament apocrypha and the Latin Vulgate. Text that the site itself marks as in copyright — the SBL Greek New Testament above all — is catalogued but not imported. The whole of the site's title index — 1,322 works — is now catalogued locally (data/imports/ccel-catalogue.json), and the importer takes each work's plain-text file (one request per work) and stores it, so the text is read without asking ccel.org again. What it does not take is recorded as a lead: works the site offers only as an ebook, works whose card names a publisher's copyright, catalogue entries whose plain-text file is the collected volume they sit in, and works the library already holds.

sources.access_method: a keyed read-only JSON API at /api/v1/ — /{text}/{ref}/moolam/, /translations/{lang}/{slug}/, /commentaries/sa/{slug}/ and /transliterations/{source_type}/{script}/, one verse a time, with an OpenAPI schema at /api/schema/; the corpus, each text's chapters and the address of every verse are published without a key at /api/texts/ and /api/texts/<CODE>/
sources.attribution_requirements: HCAL 1.1 separates three tiers. The moolam (the Sanskrit verses) is Tier A: no modern copyright attaches to it, and HCAL allows any use with courtesy attribution. The platform's Sanskrit commentaries are Tier B: they may be displayed in a non-commercial application with full attribution to the commentator, the edition and the platform. The authoritative modern translations, the modern-language commentaries and the commentary translations are Tier C: the licence gives the platform reading permission only and expressly withholds redistribution, bulk download and reproduction in third-party databases, so they are not imported into the corpus.
sources.rate_limits: The content routes require an API key, issued on an access request at /api/v1/request-access/. The server meters by the verse: moolam 1 unit, transliterations 2, AI and community translations 2, Sanskrit bhashya 3, against a daily allowance of 50 units on the Free tier, 500 on Research, 2,000 on Developer and 10,000 on a partner key, with a burst of 30 requests a minute. Every response carries a _meta block with the remaining quota, the licence identifier and a watermark. The library holds only the outline — chapters and verse addresses, which are open — and reads the text one verse at a time as a chapter is opened, at a walking pace; a corpus of 165,091 verses is far outside any daily allowance, which is the licence's intent as well as the server's limit.
sources.source_reliability_notes: The Sanskrit moolam is the received text of the Bhagavad Gita, verse by verse, in the script the reader asks for; the commentaries are the published Sanskrit bhashyas transcribed by the platform. The Gita Supersite's older hostname now redirects to Heritage IITK's verse route, so the same editions are reachable at either address.
sources.editorial_notes: Used for the Sanskrit text of the Bhagavad Gita with its chapter and verse numbering, and for the Sanskrit commentaries the platform publishes — Shankara's bhashya above all, the commentary the whole Vedanta shelf of this library reads the Gita through. Access was authorised by the project owner on 2026-10-26. Only Tier A and Tier B content is imported; the modern English and Hindi translations and commentaries that the licence withholds from third-party databases are not, and the reader shows each commentary under the commentator's name and the platform's terms rather than presenting it as this library's own. The Gita Supersite is continued at Heritage IITKanpur, which serves this corpus from the Scripture Server's API under HCAL-1.1; the importer reads the corpus, the chapters and the verse addresses from the open catalogue and holds those, and streams the verses from the content routes, which answer a key Heritage issues on request. Where a text's verse addresses are published as a sitemap they are read from it; where only per-chapter verse counts are published the addresses are built from those counts and the record says so.
sources.review_note: Approved for streamed display on 2026-10-26 against HCAL 1.1: Tier A (the Sanskrit moolam) and Tier B (the platform's Sanskrit commentaries) only. Tier C content is excluded because the licence does not extend redistribution to third-party databases.

The site asks readers not to use automated download software, and its runtime rules ask for a two-second crawl delay; both are respected, and no work is crawled twice.
sources.source_reliability_notes: A scholarly corpus of pre-modern Chinese texts with a critical apparatus: the transcribed base texts are sound, but the site's own segmentation, punctuation and any English translation are its editorial work and are credited as such. Some texts are OCR transcriptions of library scans and the site labels those as unproofed.

Access was authorised by the project owner on 2026-10-26. The Chinese text is streamed from ctext.org one chapter at a time and shown beside the translation the library already holds, each pane naming its own source.
sources.review_note: Approved for streamed display on 2026-10-26. The transcriptions are the Chinese Text Project's own editorial work and are credited on every page; requests are one chapter at a time, spaced, and never repeated for a work already imported.

The old pages are served from archive.sacred-texts.com; the site's current interface blocks scripted clients.
sources.editorial_notes: Used for Keith's Taittiriya Samhita, Part II of Thibaut's Vedanta-Sutras (SBE 38), and fifty-six complete works, including MacAuliffe's Sikh Religion, Volume 1 (1909) and Dorothy Field's Religion of the Sikhs (1914) from the archive's Sikh shelf: Darmesteter's Vendidad (SBE 4), Mills's Yasna (SBE 31), Darmesteter's Sirozahs, Yashts and Nyayis (SBE 23), West's five Pahlavi Texts volumes (SBE 5, 18, 24, 37, 47), Eggeling's Satapatha Brahmana (SBE 12, 26, 41, 43, 44), Bühler's Laws of Manu (SBE 25), Ballantyne's Sankhya Aphorisms, Pancham Sinh's Hatha Yoga Pradipika, Fausböll's Sutta-Nipata (SBE 10), Rhys Davids's Buddhist Suttas (SBE 11) and Questions of King Milinda (SBE 35–36), Cowell, Müller and Takakusu's Buddhist Mahayana Texts (SBE 49), Kern's Lotus Sutra (SBE 21), Rhys Davids and Oldenberg's Vinaya Texts (SBE 13, 17, 20), Cowell's Jataka (six volumes), and, from the archive's Christianity and Buddhism sections, the Apostolic Fathers (Ante-Nicene Fathers I), Parker's Dionysius the Areopagite, Deane's Anselm, Underhill's Cloud of Unknowing, Benham's Imitation of Christ, Strong's Udana, Rhys Davids's Psalms of the Sisters, Beal's Fo-Sho-Hing-Tsan-King (SBE 19) and Barnett's Path of Light. From the archive's Taoism shelf it carries Legge's Zhuangzi (SBE 39–40), Giles's Liezi and Yang Chu, Legge's Tai Shang Tractate, Classic of Purity, Yin Fu King and the appendixes on the Pivot of Jade and the Directory for a Day, Suzuki and Carus's Yin Chih Wen and Canon of Reason and Virtue, and Balfour's Taoist Texts and Giles's Sayings of Lao Tzŭ. From the archive's Confucianism shelf it carries the Confucian canon — the Analects with the Chinese text of the bilingual canon page, the Great Learning, the Doctrine of the Mean, Mencius, the Shû King, the religious portions of the Shih King, the Hsiâo King, both volumes of the Li Kî and the Yî King — together with Legge's 1876 Book of Poetry, Ivan Chen's Book of Filial Duty, Cranmer-Byng's Feast of Lanterns, Dawson's Ethics of Confucius, Giles's Confucianism and Its Rivals and a translation of the Shundai Zatsuwa. Access was authorised by the project owner on 2026-10-22; requests stay chapter-sized, cached, and identified by a descriptive user agent. The site's 2026 terms ask readers not to scrape or overload the service, so imports fetch once and the reader never bulk-crawls. From the archive’s Jain shelf it now carries all four works of Jacobi’s Jaina Sutras (SBE 22 and 45, 1884 and 1895) — the complete Acaranga, Kalpa Sutra, Uttaradhyayana and Sutrakritanga — read from the site’s current JSON reading views, whose printed page numbers are taken out of the text before it is shown.

sources.source_name: GRETIL — Göttingen Register of Electronic Texts in Indian Languages
sources.access_method: static files, one per work: TEI-conformant XML, an analytic HTML transformation and a plain-text transformation; the master index at gretil.html lists every entry under its language and genre
sources.attribution_requirements: Every GRETIL e-text carries a header naming the scholar who input it, the edition it follows and its licence. Credit the edition GRETIL names, the inputter and GRETIL itself. Most files in the Sanskrit corpus are distributed under CC BY-NC-SA 4.0, which forbids commercial use; individual files state their own terms and must be read before reuse.
sources.rate_limits: No API. Files are static objects; this library fetches each work once when a reader opens it, once when its passage index is built, and sends a descriptive user agent.
sources.source_reliability_notes: A curated register of Sanskrit, Pali and Prakrit e-texts, each transcribed by a named scholar from a stated printed edition. The corpus is deliberately heterogeneous: text is ASCII-transliterated, reference schemes differ from work to work, catalogues, verse-numbering and prose numbering vary, and some files interleave a commentary with the root text. Coverage is a scholarly selection, not a complete Sanskrit library, and the register is not a critical edition.
sources.editorial_notes: Used for the Sanskrit originals of the Hindu works on the Purana, Darshana, Tantra, poetics, grammar and astronomy shelves that the acquisition register had recorded as wanted with GRETIL as the lead. Works are streamed from GRETIL at read time; the library holds the catalogue record, chapter outline and passage index, and the import cache keeps the segments that were validated so the host is crawled once. Access was authorised by the project owner on 2026-10-26.

sources.attribution_requirements: Not established; Blavatsky's original works may be public domain while later editions and compilations are not.
sources.source_reliability_notes: Theosophy has multiple organisations and no single authority. Distinguish primary texts from later compilations.
sources.editorial_notes: Discovery only; verify a specific public-domain edition before import.

sources.attribution_requirements: Not established; translations and lecture transcripts have separate rights.
sources.source_reliability_notes: Large archive of Steiner's works and lectures; edition and translation provenance matter.
sources.editorial_notes: Do not treat Anthroposophy as a canon religion. Catalogue only pending rights review.

sources.organisation: Various Indigenous nations, archives and cultural centres
sources.attribution_requirements: Defined by the holding community, not by this library. Free, prior and informed consent is required.
sources.source_reliability_notes: There is no single Indigenous canon or archive. Some knowledge is restricted, ceremonial or not intended for public circulation.
sources.editorial_notes: No text imported. Any future contribution needs a community agreement, access levels, attribution and takedown process.

sources.licence_status: Tanzil text terms: verbatim copying permitted, modification not allowed
sources.attribution_requirements: Tanzil Quran Text must be reproduced verbatim and credited to the Tanzil Project. Translations carry their own terms.
sources.rate_limits: Bulk downloads supplied as files; no fixed request limit
sources.source_reliability_notes: The Uthmani text used by AlQuran Cloud and Quran.com. Every copied ayah is reproduced without modification and cites the Tanzil terms.
sources.editorial_notes: Upstream text for the Arabic Quran edition. Translations are imported separately and never mixed into the Arabic.

sources.licence_status: Unstated; individual melodies and settings carry their own rights
sources.attribution_requirements: Melody attributions and transcriptions belong to the contributors named on each entry.
sources.source_reliability_notes: A volunteer collection of Shabbat and festival zemirot with melodies. Useful for a liturgical-music shelf; not a critical edition.
sources.editorial_notes: A liturgical music section would catalogue song texts and melodies with links rather than copying audio or notation without permission.

sources.licence_status: Copyright Britain Yearly Meeting; online reading permitted, bulk copying not licensed
sources.attribution_requirements: Quaker Faith & Practice, Britain Yearly Meeting.
sources.source_reliability_notes: The authoritative current edition for Britain Yearly Meeting, searchable online.
sources.editorial_notes: Recorded as a link-out source. The library does not copy the book; extracts require permission.

sources.attribution_requirements: Cite the Dictionary entry and its author.
sources.source_reliability_notes: Scholarly biographical entries on Unitarian and Universalist figures, maintained by the UU history society.
sources.editorial_notes: Useful for author records rather than for primary texts.

sources.licence_status: Unstated; Gurbani text is public, translations and interface are not
sources.attribution_requirements: Gurbani is reproduced with its raag and ang references; translators are credited where named.
sources.source_reliability_notes: A reading interface for Sri Guru Granth Sahib with ang references and translations.
sources.editorial_notes: Prefer a source that states translation licences before importing any English text.

sources.attribution_requirements: Per document.
sources.source_reliability_notes: Scanned historical documents and pamphlets relating to Sikh history.
sources.editorial_notes: Historical documents rather than scripture; needs per-item rights review.

sources.attribution_requirements: The Rehat Maryada is issued by the SGPC; the English rendering is attributed to Dr Surjit Singh Gandhi where the PDF names him.
sources.source_reliability_notes: The official publisher of the Sikh Rehat Maryada. The Gurmukhi text is authoritative; English presentations are translations of it.
sources.editorial_notes: The governing code of the panth, but the English text carries no open licence. Catalogue and link only until permission is established.

sources.attribution_requirements: Per item; cite the holding institution and the Panjab Digital Library.
sources.rate_limits: No bulk API verified; respect the archive's terms.
sources.source_reliability_notes: Scans of Sikh manuscripts, janamsakhis, hukamnamas and nineteenth-century printed books. Most items have page images rather than searchable text, and OCR of Gurmukhi and Persian is unreliable.
sources.editorial_notes: The best route to the original-language witnesses, but the images need transcription and editorial review before any text enters the corpus. Record the manuscript or printed edition, not just the item title.

sources.attribution_requirements: Name the translator and the Society for each title.
sources.source_reliability_notes: English translations by named Sikh scholars, including Teja Singh, Kulwant Singh and Pritpal Singh Bindra. These are popular editions, not critical texts.
sources.editorial_notes: A useful lead for Bhai Gurdas's Vaaran and Kabitt Savaiyye, Sainapati's Sri Gur Sobha and the Rehat Maryada. Permission must be sought before any text is imported.

sources.access_method: web pages by ang or search; the underlying Gurbani-CD files are offered separately for download
sources.licence_status: used with written permission (permission on file)
sources.attribution_requirements: SriGranth.org and the Gurbani-CD of Kulbir S. Thind must be credited. Use of the files for internet or commercial projects requires written permission in advance; files with the English translation also require permission from Sant Singh Khalsa.
sources.rate_limits: No API. Page-by-page reading only; the site is not a crawl target.
sources.source_reliability_notes: The Gurmukhi text descends from the Gurbani-CD and is presented by ang with two English translations (Sant Singh Khalsa and Bhai Manmohan Singh), modern Punjabi, Hindi, Roman transliteration and Professor Sahib Singh's teeka. Widely used, but not a critical edition.
sources.editorial_notes: The Gurmukhi text and the Khalsa English translation were acquired under written permission from the rights holders (permission letter held by the project owner, not in the repository). The text is held locally with the permission recorded on both editions; Punjabi, Hindi, Roman and the teeka are not imported. Do not redistribute without permission.

sources.licence_status: Public-domain editions with some rights reserved by the host
sources.attribution_requirements: Cite the Japanese Text Initiative and the printed edition used.
sources.source_reliability_notes: Collaborative collection of Japanese literary and religious texts, including Kojiki and Nihon Shoki translations.
sources.editorial_notes: Candidate for the Shinto shelf; check each text's stated rights before copying.

sources.licence_status: Mixed; Blavatsky and Judge texts are public domain, later material is not
sources.attribution_requirements: Per work and author.
sources.source_reliability_notes: Organisational site with articles and some digitised early theosophical texts.
sources.editorial_notes: Public-domain Blavatsky editions are better sourced from archive.org; the society site supplies context.

sources.licence_status: Organisational material; Steiner texts have separate rights
sources.attribution_requirements: Per page.
sources.source_reliability_notes: Introductory and organisational material rather than primary texts.
sources.editorial_notes: Steiner's own works are sourced from the Rudolf Steiner Archive, not from this site.

sources.attribution_requirements: Spiritualists National Union.
sources.source_reliability_notes: Primary denominational body for UK Spiritualism; publishes principles and service texts.
sources.editorial_notes: Catalogue statements and links; service readings remain under the union's copyright.

sources.licence_status: Copyright Oomoto; English summaries offered for reading
sources.attribution_requirements: Oomoto, official English pages.
sources.source_reliability_notes: Official English pages describing the movement and its revelations.
sources.editorial_notes: Link-out only unless the movement grants permission to copy its scriptures.

sources.attribution_requirements: Seicho-no-Ie, official English pages.
sources.source_reliability_notes: Official teachings and introductory texts in English and Japanese.
sources.editorial_notes: Catalogue the movement and its texts; copying requires permission.

sources.licence_status: Mixed; each text's own rights apply
sources.attribution_requirements: Per text.
sources.source_reliability_notes: A portal reproducing public-domain and freely distributed scriptures in European languages.
sources.editorial_notes: Use as a discovery index; import from the holding edition instead of the portal.

sources.licence_status: Per volume: public domain, snippet view or in-copyright
sources.attribution_requirements: Cite the scanned edition and its library holding.
sources.source_reliability_notes: Huge scan corpus with unreliable OCR and variable view restrictions.
sources.editorial_notes: Only full-view public-domain scans could be copied; the library prefers archive.org and HathiTrust for the same books.

sources.access_method: HTTP JSON API, one chapter per request
sources.attribution_requirements: The King James Version, the Westminster Leningrad Codex and the Textus Receptus are public domain. UWL names the edition and the API on every chapter.
sources.rate_limits: Public API with no published quota; chapters are fetched on demand and cached briefly in process.
sources.source_reliability_notes: The KJV text includes Strong's numbers in markup, which are stripped for display. The Hebrew and Greek editions are served as the API holds them and have not been collated against critical editions.
sources.editorial_notes: Only the chapter and verse index is stored. Verse numbering follows the KJV; where the Hebrew counts a superscription as verse 1, the panes differ by one verse.

sources.source_type: Online edition of public-domain theological texts
sources.access_method: HTML question pages, fetched on demand
sources.attribution_requirements: The 1920 Dominican Province translation is public domain. The online edition is credited to New Advent, and UWL links back rather than copying it.
sources.rate_limits: No published limit; one question page is fetched per chapter and cached briefly in process.
sources.source_reliability_notes: The text is the second and revised edition of the Dominican Province translation (1920). New Advent states its own copyright in the online edition; UWL therefore streams rather than stores it.
sources.editorial_notes: Each question is a chapter and each article a passage. The Supplement is not Aquinas's own work and is recorded as such.

sources.access_method: JSON over HTTP; no key for read requests
sources.attribution_requirements: The Arabic commentary is a public-domain work. The host is credited on every edition and the digital text is not relicensed by this library.
sources.rate_limits: No published limit for read requests; responses are cached in the reader for ten minutes
sources.source_reliability_notes: The tafsir resources return one commentary entry per ayah with the canonical verse key, which allows the library to align the text with its own Qur'an index. Coverage is not always complete: al-Tabari's resource omits commentary on a small number of ayahs, and the reader reports a count mismatch instead of hiding it.
sources.editorial_notes: Only the catalogue record, surah outline and ayah index are stored. Arabic commentary is streamed one surah at a time. No English translation is offered because no public-domain English translation of these tafsirs was verified.

sources.attribution_requirements: The host and the named translator are credited on every edition. The repository licence covers the code and data packaging; it does not establish rights in the translations.
sources.source_reliability_notes: Section documents and hadith numbering are consistent between the Arabic and English editions of the same collection. Translator attributions are incomplete for several collections, and are recorded as unknown rather than guessed.
sources.editorial_notes: Only the catalogue record, section outline and hadith index are stored. Text is streamed section by section, so this library never holds a copy of the translations.

sources.access_method: item metadata API and the item's plain-text derivative
sources.attribution_requirements: Name the printed edition, its translator and the Internet Archive item, and keep the transcription credit (sacred-texts.com) that the text carries. The transcription asks for attribution and non-commercial reuse; the underlying 1889 text is public domain in the United States.
sources.rate_limits: Item-level access; respect the archive's terms and any lending restriction.
sources.source_reliability_notes: Only items whose printed edition is public domain and whose plain-text derivative has been read and checked are used. The first approved item is FitzGerald's Bird Parliament (1889), transcription proofed by sacred-texts.com.
sources.editorial_notes: Approval is item-level, not collection-wide. A public scan is not by itself evidence that the edition is public domain; each item must record its edition and rights check before it is imported.

sources.access_method: Raw mARkdown files over HTTPS; no key for read requests
sources.attribution_requirements: The classical work is public domain. Each digital transcription is credited to OpenITI and to the repository file it came from; the transcription is not relicensed by this library.
sources.rate_limits: GitHub raw content; no published limit for ordinary reading use
sources.source_reliability_notes: The corpus supplies machine-readable Arabic transcriptions with headings and paragraph markers. Transcription quality varies by edition: some files carry OCR or conversion artefacts, so each work here was checked for chapter structure, paragraph count and Arabic text before it was catalogued.
sources.editorial_notes: Only the catalogue record, chapter outline and passage index are stored. Text is streamed from GitHub when a chapter is opened and cached for a reading session. Arabic only: no English translation is included where no public-domain translation was verified.

sources.access_method: static HTML and PDF pages organised by tradition; transcriptions and scans of printed editions, read one page at a time
sources.attribution_requirements: Each page names its printed source. Public-domain translations (Legge, Giles, Suzuki and Carus) may be quoted with the edition credited; the modern translations hosted there (Cleary, Watson, Mair, Wong, Graham) remain in copyright and must not be copied.
sources.rate_limits: No stated limit. Read one page at a time and cache what is used, as with any static host.
sources.source_reliability_notes: A long-running personal library of Asian texts, with scans and transcriptions of public-domain and in-copyright books side by side. Its Taoism index was read item by item on 23 October 2026. The public-domain material it hosts in full — Legge's Texts of Taoism, Giles's Lieh Tzŭ, the Suzuki–Carus Kan Ying P'ien and Yin Chih Wen — is the same material already streamed from the Internet Sacred Text Archive, and its Tao Te Ching page is a bibliography of 112 translations rather than a text. Everything else on the shelf that the library lacks is a modern translation or study under copyright.
sources.editorial_notes: Reviewed twice for the Taoist shelf and not used for text. It mirrors the Legge and Giles volumes already imported from the Internet Sacred Text Archive, and its unique holdings (Watson, Mair, Graham, Cleary, Wong, Robinet, the Columbia Lieh-tzu, the 2010 Huainanzi) are in copyright. It remains a finding aid and a fallback host: the public-domain Taishang and Yin Chih Wen pages are an independent transcription of the same editions, and the Tao Te Ching index is the fullest list of English translations available, which is how the public-domain set (Legge, Balfour, Carus and Suzuki, Goddard, Medhurst, Mears, Gorn-Old, Giles) was checked for gaps. Nothing on the site was fetched into the corpus.
sources.review_note: Restricted for ingestion, not for citation. The presence of a PDF on the site is not evidence of a reusable licence; the item-by-item review found no public-domain text that is not already available from an approved host.

sources.source_name: Open Greek and Latin / Perseus Digital Library
sources.organisation: Open Greek and Latin Project (Leipzig) and Perseus Digital Library (Tufts)
sources.access_method: TEI XML files over HTTPS from the GitHub repositories First1KGreek, csel-dev, canonical-greekLit and canonical-latinLit; no key
sources.attribution_requirements: Credit the project, the repository file and the print edition it transcribes; derivatives are shared under CC BY-SA 4.0.
sources.rate_limits: GitHub raw content; no published limit for ordinary use
sources.source_reliability_notes: Each file names its print edition and editor in the TEI header. First1KGreek and Perseus files are corrected transcriptions; the csel-dev and 'opp' files are OCR transcriptions of nineteenth-century editions with the apparatus separated out, and keep occasional uncorrected OCR slips. Only files whose print edition is from before 1930 are imported, so the critical text is public domain; Loeb-based files from 1930 on are recorded in the acquisition register instead.
sources.editorial_notes: Imported 2026-11-19 by scripts/dev/import-ogl.ts: footnotes and apparatus are dropped, the top citation level becomes the chapter and the lowest becomes the passage, long passages are split at sentence ends. Text is held locally.
